findings.text: The requirement says one sentence in `public/framework/ai/sessions/readme.md`; the diff touches only `ai/AISession/readme.md`, and `sessions/readme.md` line 55 still describes "a table or rail of cards" without saying a card is four things, root sessions only.

The new AISession/readme.md bullet mixes the unrelated `classic: true` / `data_url` text with the card sentence, and it omits the new rules (rail shows roots only via `roots_for_cards`; the view toggle re-applies the grid, AISessionsPage.js ~107). A fresh agent would not find them; split into its own bullet.

"Two numbers that must agree" was met only by the first-pass log (8 rows, 6 roots, 6 drawn) from a one-off page load; no script is saved in the task folder, so nobody can re-run the count. Save the counting script in `cards/` and reference it in session.jsonl.

The child-count line was never seen drawn: the worktree lacks `session-tree.json`, and the card shots (`after-390.png`) show "6 child sessions · 10 in all" only on one card with no tree-free proof of the 0-children case beyond that. Confirm on a tree-bearing build before merge, since `roots_for_cards` silently shows every row when `AISessionRows.tree` is null.

Cost line reads "$2.37 this session · with children …" (`after-390.png`), not "$47 own · $120 with children"; it is AICost.cost_line's own wording, so it matches the "one function" ask. The "with children" part is a click-to-ask button for rows without an answer.

`roots_for_cards` drops every row that has a parent, so a child whose parent falls outside the time range (Today filter) vanishes from the rail entirely. The requirement said "filter rows whose parent is in the list"; the code filters on any parent. Tighten to parents present in `rows`.
`AISessionView.descendants` recomputes the walk per card render; fine at this size, and the "in all" count the requirements said to cut first was kept, which is harmless.
The old card showed flags and a stale "updated" age; both left the card as asked, but `flag_tags`/role chips are still defined and used in the table, so nothing is orphaned.
